## 1. Execution Context

This report provides automated quality control and visual parameter checks for the `Spring vs Winter Wheat Project` pipeline.

It is based on an aggregation of data across multiple independent `_targets` pipelines (one for each Experiment - i.e., site-year combination).

We then run a cross-pipeline quality control check across the entire set.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| echo: FALSE

library(targets)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(forcats)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(gtsummary)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)
library(plotly) 
library(readr)
library(reactable)

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
```

```{r}
#| label: extract-sim-metadata
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false
#| echo: false

# This chunk is OFF as used only to facilitate meta-data creation as original sim names do not carry obvious meta-data patterns


# Read the CSV (replace "YourFileName.csv" with your actual file path)
# Assuming the column containing the raw names is called 'SimulationName'
df_sims <- read_csv("SimulationNameByCultivarLookup.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

df_sim_metadata <- df_sims %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Extract Experiment: Grabs everything from the start up to the year
    Experiment = str_extract(SimulationName, "^.*?(2024|2025)"),
    
    # 2. Extract SeasonType: Looks for April/Apr or May
    SeasonType = case_when(
      str_detect(SimulationName, "Apr(il)?") ~ "Winter",
      str_detect(SimulationName, "May") ~ "Spring",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    
    # 3. Extract Cultivar: Handles the 4 different string formats in your data
    Cultivar = case_when(
      # Format A: Cultivar is at the end after an underscore (e.g., ..._BigRed, ..._UOM001_3_47)
      str_detect(SimulationName, "_") ~ str_extract(SimulationName, "(?<=_).*$"),
      
      # Format B: Cultivar is sandwiched between "Cv" and "Sow" (e.g., ...CvGregorySow14-May)
      str_detect(SimulationName, "Cv.*?Sow\\d") ~ str_extract(SimulationName, "(?<=Cv).*?(?=Sow)"),
      
      # Format C: Cultivar is between "SowApr/SowMay" and "PGR" (e.g., ...SowAprBigRedPGRNo)
      str_detect(SimulationName, "Sow(Apr|May).*?PGR") ~ str_extract(SimulationName, "(?<=SowApr|SowMay).*?(?=PGR)"),
      
      # Format D: Cultivar is strictly at the end of the string after "Cv" (e.g., GrassPatch2024CvGregory)
      str_detect(SimulationName, "Cv[A-Za-z]+$") ~ str_extract(SimulationName, "(?<=Cv)[A-Za-z]+$"),
      
      # Fallback just in case a new format sneaks in later
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    )
  )


#write.csv(df_sim_metadata,"SimMetaData.csv")

# Preview the beautiful new dataframe!
head(df_sim_metadata)
```

```{r}
#| label: pull-targets-func
#| include: false

# Function to safely pull targets from a specific directory store
pull_regional_data <- function(dir_name) {
  store_path <- file.path(dir_name, "_targets")
  
  if (dir.exists(store_path)) {
    
    # tryCatch will safely skip folders where the target hasn't been built yet
    tryCatch({
      tar_read_raw(target_to_pull, store = store_path) %>%
        mutate(Experiment = dir_name) # Here we BRUTE-FORCE named key for matching data to trials
    }, error = function(e) {
      warning(paste("Target", target_to_pull, "is missing inside:", dir_name))
      return(NULL)
    })
    
  } else {
    warning(paste("Targets store entirely missing for:", dir_name))
    return(NULL)
  }
}
```

## 3. Haun-related parameter checks

Currently, two APSIM parameters were manually calibrated based on a visual alignment of simulated and measured Haun stages.

- Base phyllochron: **\[Wheat\].Phenology.Phyllochron.BasePhyllochron.FixedValue**

- Photoperiod sensitivity: **\[Wheat\].Phenology.PhyllochronPpSensitivity.FixedValue**

This heuristic approach introduces uncertainty into the parameter values for any given cultivar, as these subjective estimates are prone to vary across different experimental conditions.

The subsequent analysis highlights the extent of this parameter variability.

In future stages of model development, we recommend implementing an objective, quantitative methodology to estimate best-fit parameters.

```{r}
#| label: Get-data-phyll
#| include: false

target_to_pull <- "haun_input_checked" 

# Apply function across all dirs and bind rows
df_combined_haun_param <- map_dfr(pipeline_dirs, pull_regional_data)

head(df_combined_haun_param)
```

```{r}
#| label: Clean-data-haun
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false

# Join the lookup table to our combined data
# We use left_join so we don't lose any data if a name is missing from the lookup
df_final <- df_combined_haun_param %>%
  dplyr::select(-Experiment)%>% # info is already in SimName and crashes due to duplication
  left_join(sim_name_lookup_table, by = "SimulationName") %>%
  mutate(
    Cultivar = factor(Cultivar), 
    Experiment = factor(Experiment)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-SimulationName)

# Check if any rows failed to match a cultivar
missing_cultivars <- df_final %>% filter(is.na(Cultivar))
if(nrow(missing_cultivars) > 0) {
  warning("Some SimulationNames did not have a matching Cultivar in the lookup table.")
}

```

### Base Phyllochron parameter analysis

This plot checks the spread of the base phyllochron parameter across all simulated cultivars. The gray bars show the absolute min/max range, the red 'X' marks the MEDIAN, and the colored dots represent individual Experiments simulations as in @fig-graph-phyllo

```{r}
#| label: fig-graph-phyllo
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of Phyllochron values by Cultivar assumed across Experiments"
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 10
#| warning: false

this_variable <- "[Wheat].Phenology.Phyllochron.BasePhyllochron.FixedValue"

# 1. Pre-calculate the min, max, and median for each Cultivar
df_summary <- df_final %>%
  group_by(Cultivar) %>%
  summarize(
    min_val = min(.data[[this_variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
    max_val = max(.data[[this_variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
    #mod_val = mode(.data[[this_variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
    med_val = median(.data[[this_variable]], na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# 2. Reorder Cultivar as a factor based on the median (so the plot sorts correctly)
df_final <- df_final %>%
  mutate(Cultivar = fct_reorder(Cultivar, .data[[this_variable]], .fun = median, .na_rm = TRUE))

df_summary <- df_summary %>%
  mutate(Cultivar = factor(Cultivar, levels = levels(df_final$Cultivar)))

# 3. Build the plot using basic geoms that plotly understands
p <- ggplot() + 
  # Min-Max range (using geom_segment instead of linerange for better plotly translation)
  geom_segment(
    data = df_summary,
    aes(y = Cultivar, yend = Cultivar, x = min_val, xend = max_val),
    linewidth = 4, color = "grey25", alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  # Jittered points colored by Experiment
  geom_jitter(
    data = df_final,
    aes(
      y = Cultivar, 
      x = .data[[this_variable]], 
      color = Experiment,
      text = Experiment # Helps format the hover tooltip
    ),
    height = 0.2, width = 0, alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  # Median marker
  geom_point(
    data = df_summary,
    aes(y = Cultivar, x = med_val),
    shape = 4, color = "red", size = 2, stroke = 1
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  labs(
    y = "Cultivar", 
    x = "Base Phyllochron (Fixed Value)"
  ) 

# 4. Convert it to an interactive graph
ggplotly(p, tooltip = c("x", "text"))
```

## 4.Biomass component checks

In this project, by definition, we are assuming total above ground biomass (Wheat.AboveGround.Wt) composition as below:

- **Wheat.AboveGround.Wt** = Wheat.Leaf.Live.Wt + Wheat.Leaf.Dead.Wt + Wheat.Stem.Wt + Wheat.Spike.Wt + Wheat.Grain.Wt

Note that, terminology-wise, *Ear* in APSIM is the same as chaff (i.e., without grains). So:

- **Wheat.Ear.Wt** = Wheat.Spike.Wt + Wheat.Grain.Wt

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: Get-data-bio

target_to_pull <- "qc_obs_final" 

# Apply function across all dirs and bind rows
df_combined_bio_raw <- map_dfr(pipeline_dirs, pull_regional_data)
```

The ranges of different biomass components for each Experiment can be checked at @tbl-Get-data-bio2.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-Get-data-bio2
#| message: false


df_combined_bio <- df_combined_bio_raw %>%
  dplyr::select(-Experiment)  %>%
  left_join(sim_name_lookup_table, by = "SimulationName") %>%
  mutate(
    Cultivar = factor(Cultivar), 
    Experiment = factor(Experiment)
  ) 

# 2. Define the essential variables needed for your biomass calculations and plots
essential_vars <- c(
  "Experiment",
  "SimulationName",
  "Wheat.AboveGround.Wt", 
  "Wheat.Leaf.Live.Wt", 
  "Wheat.Leaf.Dead.Wt", 
  "Wheat.Stem.Wt", 
  "Wheat.Spike.Wt", 
  "Wheat.Ear.Wt", 
  "Wheat.Grain.Wt"
)

# 3. Check for missing variables and throw a warning if any are not found
missing_vars <- setdiff(essential_vars, colnames(df_combined_bio))
if (length(missing_vars) > 0) {
  warning(paste(
    "The following essential variables were missing from the pulled data:", 
    paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", ")
  ))
}

# 4. Pre-select only the essential variables 
# (any_of ensures the code won't crash if a variable is missing)
df_combined_bio <- df_combined_bio %>%
  select(any_of(essential_vars))

# 5. Print a beautifully formatted summary table grouped by Experiment
df_combined_bio %>%
  dplyr::select(-SimulationName) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = Experiment, 
    missing = "no", # Removes the 'Unknown' NA rows entirely
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "({min}, {max})" # Removes the median, leaving only the range
    ),
    label = list(
      any_of("Wheat.AboveGround.Wt") ~ "Above Ground Wt",
      any_of("Wheat.Leaf.Live.Wt") ~ "Live Leaf Wt",
      any_of("Wheat.Leaf.Dead.Wt") ~ "Dead Leaf Wt",
      any_of("Wheat.Stem.Wt") ~ "Stem Wt",
      any_of("Wheat.Spike.Wt") ~ "Spike Wt",
      any_of("Wheat.Ear.Wt") ~ "Ear Wt",
      any_of("Wheat.Grain.Wt") ~ "Grain Wt"
    )
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  modify_caption("**Summary Statistics of Biomass Components by Experiment**")
```

To test the alignment of the diverse raw-data terminology across the data pipeline, we here cross-check **biomass-component sums** with reported **Wheat.AboveGround.Wt in the raw-data** across all final **Observed.xlsx** used to test simulations (@fig-graph-bio1).

```{r}
#| label: fig-graph-bio1
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of Above-Ground sums vs. Observed values across simulations.The 1:1 line in red."
#| echo: false
#| message: false

df_plot <- df_combined_bio %>%
  mutate(
    Spike_Plus_Grain = coalesce(Wheat.Spike.Wt, 0) + coalesce(Wheat.Grain.Wt, 0),
    TotalBiomassComponentSum = 
      coalesce(Wheat.Leaf.Live.Wt, 0) +
      coalesce(Wheat.Leaf.Dead.Wt, 0) +
      coalesce(Wheat.Stem.Wt, 0) +
      coalesce(Wheat.Spike.Wt, 0) +
      coalesce(Wheat.Ear.Wt, 0) +
      coalesce(Wheat.Grain.Wt, 0)
  ) %>%
  
  # Extract everything from the start of the string up to and including 2024 or 2025
  mutate(SimName = str_extract(SimulationName, "^.*?(2024|2025)")) 

# 1. Save your ggplot as an object 'p'
p <- df_plot %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Wheat.AboveGround.Wt, 
             y = TotalBiomassComponentSum,
             colour = SimName)) + 
  geom_point() +
  # Adding the 1:1 line since you are doing validation!
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal()

# 2. Convert it to an interactive graph
ggplotly(p)

```

### 5. Phenology parameter check

Similar to Haun-related parameters, phenology was **forced-as-input** to perfectly match observations. 

For that, dates of pheno-stages were extracted from raw data, calculated from Haun-index or interpolated (@tbl-pheno-method). 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pheno-method
#| tbl-cap: "APSIM Phenology Stage Parameters and Data Sources"
#| message: false
#| echo: false
```


| Stage | ParameterNameAPSIM | DataSource | RawDataEvent |
|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|
| 2 | \[Wheat\].Phenology.Germinating.DateToProgress | Assumed post-sow | Instant Germination |
| 3 | \[Wheat\].Phenology.Emerging.DateToProgress | Raw data | 50% Emergence |
| 4 | \[Wheat\].Phenology.LeavesInitiating.DateToProgress | Haun-index derived | see calc below |
| 5 | \[Wheat\].Phenology.SpikeletsDifferentiating.DateToProgress | Haun-index derived | see calc below |
| 6 | \[Wheat\].Phenology.StemElongating.DateToProgress | Raw data | 50% Flag leaves PCDS 6.0 |
| 7 | \[Wheat\].Phenology.Heading.DateToProgress | Interpolation_6_8 | 50% interpolation |
| 8 | \[Wheat\].Phenology.Flowering.DateToProgress | Raw data | 50% Anthesis PCDS 8.0 |
| 10 | \[Wheat\].Phenology.GrainFilling.DateToProgress | Raw data | date when available |

#### Haun-based estimation of dates for stages 4 and 5

a.  Final Leaf Number (FLN) and target leaf-number estimation

The Final Leaf Number is calculated by finding the maximum observed Haun stage in the dataset and rounding it to the nearest whole integer.The date for FLN was assumed at a close earlier (defaulting to 0.95FLN) to avoid confounding with multiple dates when a similar (or very close) maximum leaf number was measured. 

$$Haun_{limit} = \max(Haun_{obs}) \times c_{limit}$$
`<!-- -->`{=html}b. Double Ridge date date estimation

The *Double Ridge date (APSIM Stage 4)* is assumed to occur six leaf stages prior to the Final Leaf Number date, with a hard floor set at Haun stage 2 to prevent biologically impossible negative stages.
$$Haun_{DR} = \max(2, FLN - 6)$$


`<!-- -->`{=html}c. Terminal Spikelet date estimation 

The *Terminal Spikelet date (APSIM Stage 5)* is assumed to occur exactly three leaf stages prior to the Final Leaf Number.
$$Haun_{TS} = FLN - 3$$
The resulting phenology date windows estimated for each APSIM PhaseName are shown in @tbl-pheno-summary.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pheno-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Ranges of dates for each Experiment and APSIM phase name."
#| message: false
#| echo: false
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r}
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(knitr)

target_to_pull <- "df_pheno_input_param" 

# ---- 1. Apply function across all dirs and bind rows ----
df_combined_pheno_param <- map_dfr(pipeline_dirs, pull_regional_data)

# ---- 2. Clean data and parse dates ----
df_final <- df_combined_pheno_param %>%
  dplyr::select(-Experiment) %>%
  left_join(sim_name_lookup_table, by = "SimulationName") %>%
  mutate(
    Cultivar = factor(Cultivar), 
    Experiment = factor(Experiment),
    SeasonType = factor(SeasonType) # Ensure SeasonType is a clean factor
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(contains("DateToProgress"), dmy)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-SimulationName)

# ---- 3. Reshape, group, and pivot Seasons side-by-side ----
df_pheno_summary <- df_final %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = contains("DateToProgress"),
    names_to = "Phase",
    values_to = "Date"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Date)) %>%
  mutate(
    Phase = str_remove_all(Phase, "\\[Wheat\\]\\.Phenology\\.|\\.DateToProgress")
  ) %>%
  # Group by Experiment, SeasonType, AND Phase to split the math
  group_by(Experiment, SeasonType, Phase) %>%
  summarise(
    Min_Date = min(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max_Date = max(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Min_Date = format(Min_Date, "%d-%b-%Y"),
    Max_Date = format(Max_Date, "%d-%b-%Y")
  ) %>%
  # Rename the variables before pivoting so the final column names look professional
  rename(
    `Earliest` = Min_Date,
    `Latest` = Max_Date
  ) %>%
  # Pivot wide: this creates columns like "Winter Earliest", "Spring Latest", etc.
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = SeasonType,
    values_from = c(`Earliest`, `Latest`),
    names_glue = "{SeasonType} {.value}"
  ) %>%
  # Dynamically order the columns (handles cases where a season might be missing)
  dplyr::select(Experiment, Phase, contains("Winter"), contains("Spring"))

# ---- 4. Loop through experiments to build Tabset Tables ----
experiments <- unique(df_pheno_summary$Experiment)

for (exp in experiments) {
  
  cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n", exp))
  
  df_sub <- df_pheno_summary %>%
    filter(Experiment == exp) %>%
    dplyr::select(-Experiment)
  
  # Generate the kable table using markdown format for safe 'asis' rendering
  # Using rep("c", ncol(df_sub) - 1) automatically adjusts alignment based on column count
  k_tbl <- kable(
    df_sub, 
    align = c("l", rep("c", ncol(df_sub) - 1)),
    format = "markdown"
  )
  
  print(k_tbl)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

:::

The full progression of observed and estimated pheno stages is shown in @fig-graph-pheno-tabs.

```{r}
#| label: fig-graph-pheno-tabs2
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: asis

# 0. Define the lookup table mapping stages to their data sources
stage_source_map <- data.frame(
  Stage = c("Emerging", "LeavesInitiating", "SpikeletsDifferentiating", "StemElongating", "Heading", "Flowering", "GrainFilling"),
  Source = c("DataRaw", "HaunCalc", "HaunCalc", "DataRaw", "InterpCalc", "DataRaw", "DataRaw")
)

# 1. Extract the chronological order directly from the original dataframe's columns
stage_levels <- df_final %>%
  select(contains("DateToProgress")) %>%
  names() %>%
  str_remove_all("\\[Wheat\\]\\.Phenology\\.|\\.DateToProgress")

# 2. Reshape the data from wide to long and join the source metadata
df_pheno_long <- df_final %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = contains("DateToProgress"),
    names_to = "Stage",
    values_to = "Date"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Date)) %>%
  mutate(
    Stage = str_remove_all(Stage, "\\[Wheat\\]\\.Phenology\\.|\\.DateToProgress"),
    Stage = factor(Stage, levels = stage_levels)
  ) %>%
  left_join(stage_source_map, by = "Stage") %>%
  mutate(Source = coalesce(Source, "Unknown"))

# 3. & 4. Loop through experiments and build interactive plots inside tabs
experiments <- unique(df_pheno_long$Experiment)

for (exp in experiments) {
  
  cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n", exp))
  
  df_sub <- df_pheno_long %>% filter(Experiment == exp)
  
  # DYNAMIC HEIGHT CALCULATION: 
  # Assign ~25 pixels of vertical space per unique cultivar to prevent compression, 
  # plus 200 pixels for the legend and axis text. Ensure a minimum height of 500px.
  n_cultivars <- length(unique(df_sub$Cultivar))
  dynamic_height <- max(500, (n_cultivars * 25) + 200)
  
  # Build the ggplot
  p_sub <- ggplot(df_sub, aes(
      x = Date, 
      y = Cultivar, 
      color = Stage,
      shape = Source,
      text = paste("Cultivar:", Cultivar, "<br>Stage:", Stage, "<br>Date:", format(Date, "%d-%b"), "<br>Source:", Source)
    )) +
    geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
    
    # CRITICAL CHANGE: 'free_x' locks the Y-axis so Cultivars align horizontally, 
    # but frees the X-axis so dates can shift for Winter vs. Spring.
    facet_wrap(~SeasonType, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
    
    scale_x_date(date_labels = "%d-%b") +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      x = "Date",
      y = "Cultivar",
      color = "Phenological Stage",
      shape = "Data Source"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      legend.position = "bottom" 
    )
  
  # Apply the dynamically calculated height to the Plotly widget
  plt <- ggplotly(p_sub, tooltip = "text", height = dynamic_height) %>%
    layout(
      legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.15),
      margin = list(b = 80)
    )
  
  print(htmltools::tagList(plt))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## 6. Management data

Within each *.apsimx* simulation **ALL** the management should be only within two nodes (**ManagementWinter and ManagementSpring**).

Please advise if any other auto-management script left-over is found for water and N fertiliser applications.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-management-head
#| tbl-cap: "Extract of management data to check"
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| include: false

# All extracted data is shown in @tbl-management-head

library(jsonlite)
library(purrr)
library(dplyr)
library(reactable) # Added for the table

# 1. Define the folder containing your .apsimx files
# (Update this path if it's different!)
apsimx_dir <- "C:/github/ApsimX/Tests/Validation/Wheat/UoM_WinterVsSpring" 

apsimx_files <- list.files(
  path = apsimx_dir, 
  pattern = "\\.apsimx$", 
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive = TRUE
)

# 2. Helper function: Recursively hunt for nodes by their EXACT "Name"
find_management_nodes <- function(node, target_names) {
  found_nodes <- list()
  
  # If the current node matches one of our target names, grab it
  if (!is.null(node$Name) && node$Name %in% target_names) {
    found_nodes <- append(found_nodes, list(node))
  }
  
  # Keep digging through Children if they exist
  if (!is.null(node$Children)) {
    child_results <- map(node$Children, ~find_management_nodes(.x, target_names))
    
    # Use base R 'do.call(c, ...)' to safely combine the lists 
    # instead of flatten() to avoid package conflicts!
    found_nodes <- append(found_nodes, do.call(c, child_results))
  }
  
  return(found_nodes)
}

# 3. Main function: Extract operations from a single file
extract_operations <- function(file_path) {
  raw_json <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file_path, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  
  # Search for the two specific management nodes
  target_nodes <- find_management_nodes(
    raw_json, 
    c("ManagementWinter", "ManagementSpring")
  )
  
  if (length(target_nodes) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  # Loop through found nodes and extract the 'Line' from the OperationsList
  map_dfr(target_nodes, function(node) {
    
    # Safety check: ensure OperationsList actually has items
   if (is.null(node$OperationsList) || length(node$OperationsList) == 0) {
      return(NULL) 
    }
    
    # Map over the OperationsList and pull out just the "Line" string
    extracted_lines <- map_chr(node$OperationsList, function(op) {
      if (!is.null(op$Line)) return(op$Line)
      return(NA_character_)
    })
    
    # Return as a neat tibble
    tibble(
      Management_Type = node$Name,
      Operation_Line = extracted_lines
    )
  })
}

# 4. Execute across all files and bind into a single dataframe!
df_management_ops <- apsimx_files %>%
  set_names(basename(apsimx_files)) %>% 
  map_dfr(~extract_operations(.x), .id = "Source.File") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Operation_Line)) # Clean up any empty ones

# 5. Output the full dataset as an interactive, paginated table
reactable(
  df_management_ops,
  defaultPageSize = 5,  # Keeps it small on the screen
  searchable = TRUE,    # Lets you easily search for specific operations
  striped = TRUE,
  highlight = TRUE,
  compact = TRUE,
  wrap = FALSE,         # Prevents long APSIM operation lines from wrapping
  resizable = TRUE      # Lets the reader expand column widths
)
```

Individual **Experiments** and **SimulationNames** can be checked here in @tbl-management

## 7. Pipeline log warnings

During the data wrangling process there are multiple calculations and data cleaning that involve assumptions. 

Warnings are produced at these steps to enable later scrutiny and corrections where needed.

Please **CHECK CAREFULLY** these messages for each experiment (@tbl-pipeline-health).

For items that feel relevant to you, please go to the full **pipeline_log.txt** at the Experiment folder for details.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pipeline-health
#| tbl-cap: "Pipeline Execution Health & Warnings Summary"
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(reactable)

extract_qflags <- function(log_path) {
  log_text <- readLines(log_path, warn = FALSE)
  
  # 1. Grab Experiment Name
  proj_idx <- which(str_detect(log_text, "\\$proj_name"))
  experiment_name <- if (length(proj_idx) > 0) {
    str_extract(log_text[proj_idx + 1], '(?<=").*?(?=")')
  } else {
    basename(dirname(log_path)) 
  }
  
  # 2. Extract ONLY the lines containing "[Q-FLAG]"
  qflag_lines <- log_text[str_detect(log_text, "^\\[Q-FLAG\\]")]
  
  # 3. If the log is clean (no flags), return a Pass
  if (length(qflag_lines) == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      Experiment = experiment_name, 
      Severity = "✅ PASS", 
      Category = "CLEAN", 
      Message = "No critical warnings or automated fixes detected."
    ))
  }
  
  # 4. Magically split the structured string into neat columns!
  tibble(raw_text = qflag_lines) %>%
    separate(
      col = raw_text,
      into = c("Flag", "Severity", "Category", "Message"),
      sep = "\\s*\\|\\s*", # Splits exactly at the '|' and trims whitespace
      extra = "merge"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Experiment = experiment_name,
      # Add emojis dynamically based on severity!
      Severity = case_when(
        Severity == "FATAL" ~ "🚨 FATAL",
        Severity == "CRITICAL" ~ "🚨 CRITICAL",
        Severity == "WARN" ~ "⚠️ WARN",
        Severity == "INFO" ~ "ℹ️ INFO",
        TRUE ~ Severity
      )
    ) %>%
    select(Experiment, Severity, Category, Message)
}

# 2. Define locations
base_dir <- "C:/github/ApsimX/Tests/Validation/Wheat/UoM_WinterVsSpring"
pipeline_dirs <- c(
  "Dookie2024", "Dookie2025", "Fords2025", 
  "Gnarwarre2024", "Gnarwarre2025", "GrassPatch2024", 
  "GrassPatch2025", "Turretfield2024", "WaggaWagga2024", "WaggaWagga2025"
)

# 3. Build paths and filter to only those that exist
log_files <- file.path(base_dir, pipeline_dirs, "pipeline_log.txt")
valid_log_files <- log_files[file.exists(log_files)]

# 4. Extract issues and bind into one master dataframe
df_pipeline_health <- map_dfr(valid_log_files, extract_qflags)

# 5. Render the grouped interactive table
reactable(
  df_pipeline_health,
  searchable = TRUE,
  filterable = TRUE,
  groupBy = "Experiment", 
  striped = TRUE,
  compact = TRUE,
  defaultColDef = colDef(minWidth = 150),
  columns = list(
    Experiment = colDef(minWidth = 200, name = "Experiment / Pipeline"),
    Severity = colDef(minWidth = 150, name = "Severity Level", align = "center"),
    Category = colDef(minWidth = 150, name = "Category"),
    Message = colDef(minWidth = 400, name = "Action Item / Description")
  )
)
```
